summary: Open imaging data cover the measurable part of the claim piecemeal: IDR holds centriole-number perturbation screens (PLK4, 1,539 images) and centrosome-localization phenotypes (414 images); the BioImage Archive has a 900 GB CC0 live-tracking set of centrosome size oscillating across Drosophila nuclear cycles (S-BIAD988) and two acentrosomal oocyte-spindle studies. No dataset is designed around de novo centrosome formation after loss, and plant acentriolar division is absent from these archives, so the 'disappear and form anew' and 'cells without visible centrosomes' clauses need study-by-study assembly. The 'centre of force' clause has no dataset-measurable variable.
next_step: Define 'visible centrosome' operationally (marker + resolution), then score presence/absence and aster formation per frame in S-BIAD988 and in the PLK4-depletion IDR images; add a plant mitosis time-lapse from BIA if one can be found with a γ-tubulin marker.
obstacles_confirmed: Absence of visible material depends on detection sensitivity.
Plant spindles without centrioles still have microtubule-organising material (no plant dataset located here).
'Essentially a centre of force' does not specify a force to measure.
